title: The computer and the tablet
summary: The machines the shop runs on in Supermarket Simulator are hardware as well as screens: the game keeps a computer object with its own interaction and a system with a desktop behind it, and it ships a tablet device with a scanner icon.
body: The shop's computer is a thing in the room before it is a menu. There is a computer object and an interaction belonging to it, which is how the game can let you walk up to it and use it rather than only opening a screen.

Behind the screens there is a system. The game keeps an operating system of its own and a generic desktop, so what you see on the computer is drawn by something with a desktop rather than being a set of unrelated panels.
The game also ships a tablet: there is a tablet device in its own right, and the tablet carries a cart item, so a handheld machine is modelled rather than being the same object as the desk computer.

The screens can be moved through. There is a swipe controller in the build, so stepping between panels on a touch screen is a gesture the game handles rather than something each panel does for itself.

Orders reach the shop through customers of their own. There is a generator for them, a map item for showing one, and a networked form, which is why an online order can be tracked as a customer walking in rather than only as a line in a list.
The machines have their own look. The game ships a texture for the tablet and a scanner icon for it, which is what the handheld's screen and its scanning side are drawn from.
The two pictures beside this entry are the game's own: the tablet's texture and the icon it uses for scanning.
What this entry does not tell you: how many screens the computer has, what the tablet is for, or what any of it costs. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The computer is an object with an interaction of its own.
It runs a system of its own, with a desktop.
The game has a tablet device of its own.
The tablet carries a cart item.
Orders bring customers that are generated, shown on the map and kept in a networked form.
The game ships a texture for the tablet and a scanner icon for it.
The build keeps a swipe controller of its own.
The build ships materials for the shop computer and for a low-resolution checkout screen.
The device screens name a background of their own and an input-field background.
The tablet itself has a colour sheet, a normal map and a metallic-smoothness sheet.
The build ships numbered icons for its own apps and activities.
